ai.description: This large, slender colubrid reaches 2.5 meters. It is reddish-brown with dark, white-edged crossbands and a distinct, dark Y-shaped mark on the head. It features vertical pupils and a prehensile tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Boiga forsteni* is best distinguished by its large size and the presence of a distinct, dark Y-shaped or V-shaped mark on the nape, contrasting with its reddish-brown body.
ai.habitat: *Boiga forsteni* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests, often found in dense vegetation or tree hollows across elevations ranging from sea level to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Reddish Peninsular Cat Snake is primarily nocturnal and arboreal, often using its prehensile tail to anchor itself while hunting birds and small mammals in trees.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Boiga forsteni* is oviparous, laying clutches of 7–15 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (April to August) in India.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Boiga forsteni* is found across peninsular India, primarily in the Western Ghats and central regions, ranging from sea level up to approximately 1,500 meters elevation.
